title: React Mastery Test
description: Test your mastery of React 18+: JSX, Hooks, reconciliation, context, custom hooks, and performance optimization.

questions.question: What is JSX in React?
options: A JavaScript syntax extension allowing HTML-like template syntax to be written directly in JavaScript code
A standalone database query language
A CSS preprocessor framework like Sass
A server-side Node.js routing library
questions.explanation: JSX compiles down to `React.createElement()` or `_jsx()` function calls creating plain JavaScript objects representing UI elements.

questions.question: What is the primary rule regarding the order of React Hook calls inside a functional component?
options: Hooks must be called at the top level of the component and never inside loops, conditions, or nested functions
Hooks must always be called inside a `try...catch` block
Hooks can only be called inside class component lifecycle methods
Hooks must be passed as props to child components
questions.explanation: React relies on the call order of hooks across renders to match up internal hook states with components.

questions.question: What is the difference between `useMemo` and `useCallback`?
options: `useMemo` memoizes the calculated result of a function; `useCallback` memoizes the function definition itself to prevent unnecessary child re-renders
`useCallback` executes asynchronously while `useMemo` is synchronous
`useMemo` is used for API fetching only
`useCallback` replaces the `useState` hook
questions.explanation: `useMemo(() => computeVal(a), [a])` caches values, whereas `useCallback(fn, deps)` caches callback function references.

questions.question: In React 18, what does Automatic Batching mean?
options: React groups multiple state updates (including those inside promises, setTimeout, or event handlers) into a single re-render for performance
React compiles all components into a single file at runtime
React batches network fetch requests automatically
React merges all CSS files into one stylesheet
questions.explanation: React 18 batches all state updates regardless of origin (promises, native events, timeouts), reducing redundant intermediate renders.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `useRef` in React beyond accessing DOM elements?
options: Storing mutable values that persist across renders without triggering a component re-render when mutated
Creating global application state across all routes
Triggering component re-renders when data changes
Managing CSS media queries
questions.explanation: Mutating `.current` on a ref does not cause a re-render, making it ideal for storing timer IDs, previous state values, and instance flags.

questions.question: What happens when you call `setState` with the same primitive value as current state (`setCount(5)` when count is already 5)?
options: React bails out (skips re-rendering the component and its children) using Object.is comparison
React throws an InfiniteLoopError
React force re-renders all parent components
React resets the state to 0
questions.explanation: React checks state changes with `Object.is`. If the new value is identical to current state, React skips re-rendering children.

questions.question: What is the purpose of React Error Boundaries?
options: Class components that catch JavaScript errors in their child component tree, log them, and display a fallback UI instead of crashing the app
A hook that catches syntax errors at compile time
A network proxy that intercepts 500 internal server errors
A CSS wrapper that prevents layout shift
questions.explanation: Error boundaries (`componentDidCatch` / `getDerivedStateFromError`) catch unhandled rendering exceptions, preventing entire app white-screens.

questions.question: What is 'Prop Drilling' in React and what is the primary way to solve it?
options: Passing props down through many nested intermediary components that do not need them; solved by React Context or global state managers (Zustand/Redux)
Drilling holes into virtual DOM nodes to improve speed
Validating props with TypeScript interfaces
Passing functions instead of objects as props
questions.explanation: Prop drilling clutters intermediate component signatures; Context API or state libraries allow components to consume state directly without intermediate passthroughs.

questions.question: What does the `useTransition` hook introduced in React 18 allow developers to do?
options: Mark non-urgent state updates as transitions that can be interrupted by urgent user interactions (like typing in an input)
Animate CSS transitions between pages
Navigate between React Router routes
Migrate class components to functional components
questions.explanation: `useTransition` lets you prioritize responsive user input (urgent) over heavy filtering/rendering operations (transitions) without freezing the UI.

questions.question: Why should you never mutate state directly in React (e.g. `items.push(newItem)`)?
options: Direct mutations bypass React's state comparison checks, leading to missed re-renders, stale UI, and broken time-travel debugging
Direct mutation crashes the browser memory
Direct mutation converts arrays to strings
JavaScript does not allow modifying objects
questions.explanation: React compares object references; mutating an array in-place keeps the same reference, preventing React from detecting state changes.
